title: Handoff microkernel signal extraction weekly digest
body:
Context: quick weekly digest from the handoff tabletop focused on extracting signals out of the microkernel and how those signals should drive KV cache heuristics and batch routing. This doc captures what we observed during the late-night prefills on 06/12–06/14, short experiment summaries, and concrete next actions for the oncall and kernel teams.

Highlights and emergent patterns:
- Signal drift after idle windows: observed ~12% increase in tail latency for requests that hit an idle kernel for >15s. Likely cause: cold KV window + kernel mmap rewarm. Hypothesis: a soft-warm path avoiding full prefill for short sessions reduces tail by ~8–10%. Ticket: JIRA-7891.
- Micro-sampler bias: sampler that seeds cohort buckets picks too many short-context requests during 00:00–04:00 UTC, skewing batch composition and reducing average batch length. Result: batching efficiency down by 6% on the night-shift slice. Action: tweak sampler weight by time-of-day bucket.
- Out-of-order prefill arrivals: we saw a pattern where prefill ops were enqueued but applied after user request, causing wasted KV fills. Root cause: race in the prefill coordinator where prefill ack depends on tokenization completion. Quick mitigation: move prefill ack to prefactor stage (non-blocking). See PR#4521.
- Drop-in kernel handshake regression: a recent inbound kernel handshake change reduced fast-path admissions under high concurrency; metrics show a drop in admitted continuous batches per-second from 920 -> 860 under synthetic load. Rollback candidate scoped to handshake backoff change (revert knob: handshake_fastpath_disable).

Experiments run this week (summary):
- Experiment A: soft-warm prefill flow (canary on 5% of prefills)
  - Setup: enable soft-warm path for prefills where prior kernel used <60% utilization in last 60s.
  - Observed: median latency -3ms, 95th -7ms for impacted requests, cost delta +0.4% (prefill ops increased).
  - Decision: expand to 15% and monitor KV hit-rate.

- Experiment B: time-biased sampler weights
  - Setup: night window (00:00–06:00 UTC) sampler weight reduced by 25% for short-context clients.
  - Observed: batching efficiency improved from 74% -> 79% in window; small increase in median latency for short interactive sessions (+1ms).
  - Decision: keep as temporary tweak; track false negatives (requests that should've been sampled).

Operational notes / incidents:
- 2026-06-13 02:17 UTC: brief surge related to marketing campaign; prefill backlog grew to 3.4k tasks queued; backlog cleared after horizontal bursting but we saw a 12% eviction rate for thin-state KV. Postmortem in progress (owner: Priya).
- Night-handoff friction: incomplete runbook steps around prefills applied vs committed — oncall had to escalate to kernel team twice. Need clearer signal in Console (prefill state labels: queued -> in_progress -> applied -> committed).

Open questions and hypotheses to validate:
- Are we filling too aggressively for short-lived traces? Quantify how many prefills never get reused (wasted ops) by cohort over 24h. (Owner: Evan)
- Can we add a lightweight 'prefill score' produced by the sampler that the scheduler can use to deprioritize speculative fills under pressure? (Spike: 2d, owner: Marcus)
- What's the interaction between KV TTL heuristics and microkernel eviction scheduling when thermal throttling occurs? Early signal: TTL-based compaction triggered more evictions during high-temp windows. (Owner: Sofia)

Action items (short):
- Priya: complete backlog postmortem and propose a priority-queue mitigation for prefills (due 06/20).
- Marcus: prototype sampler score field and a matching scheduler filter (spike 06/21–06/22).
- Evan: produce daily chart of prefill reuse rate by client cohort, start with last 14 days (due 06/19).
- Anita: open a rollback PR for the handshake knob if canary on v2 shows further drop under synthetic stressing (owner: Anita/Oncall).
- Kernel team: add non-blocking prefill ack in PR#4521 and request review (blocked on infra test harness).

Practical checklist for night shift (short):
- If prefill queue > 2k: flip burst-cap to +1 instance pool and set sampler conservative mode.
- If KV eviction rate > 10% sustained for 10m: enable thinstate-protect mode and notify SRE.
- If admitted batch rate drops > 5% baseline: check handshake_fastpath_disable flag and rollback to previous value.

Notes-to-self / things to remember:
- Keep experiment cohorts small and tag prefills with experiment id so we can slice reuse rates.
- Add a one-line description field to each prefill log entry — makes triage faster.
- Cross-link runbooks to Console alerts (prefill-backlog, kv-eviction).

Meeting attendees: Anita (owner), Marcus, Priya, Evan, Sofia, Kunal (SRE), Rebecca (oncall).

Next sync: short triage on 2026-06-18 09:30 PT to review experiment expansion metrics and night-handoff checklist items.

Appendix (quick refs):
- Log snippet: 2026-06-13T02:21:14Z prefill-coordinator: queued=3421 applied=2905 committed=2210 evicted=411
- Metric pointers: metric.kv.eviction_rate, metric.prefill.reuse_rate, metric.batch.admitted_per_sec

If anything here looks off or you saw different numbers during your run, paste raw traces into the thread and tag me.
